summary: An invitation site for a wedding, engagement or other private celebration: the invitation itself, the couple's story, the programme and practical details (map, travel, where to stay, dress code, gifts, FAQ) and a per-guest RSVP flow.

pages.purpose: The invitation: who is getting married, when and where, the story, the weekend at a glance and the call to reply.

sections.purpose: An arched or framed photo beside a typeset invitation card: hosts, names, day, date, time, place and the reply action.
alternatives: media-text: photo and invitation text side by side when no full hero is wanted
sections.notes: Primary action 'Reply to the invitation', secondary 'The weekend'. A countdown to the day is optional and must not be the only place the date appears.

fields: Date and time of the ceremony with time zone

sections.purpose: How the couple got here, in a few dated moments.
alternatives: media-text: one paragraph beside a photo

sections.purpose: The days of the celebration at a glance (welcome evening, ceremony, brunch), linking to details.
fields: Each day: name, theme, time, place

sections.purpose: The venue in a picture and a few lines, linking to the map and travel.
fields: What it is like and how far from town

sections.purpose: A short, warm note on gifts, so guests do not have to ask.
A closing band with the reply-by date and the RSVP action.

pages.purpose: Everything a guest needs: the full programme, the map, getting there, where to stay, what to wear, gifts and questions.

sections.purpose: Key facts at the top: ceremony date and time, place, dress code, reply-by.
The programme per day with times and an icon per event, key moments marked.
fields: Per event: day, start time, title, place, short note (transport, what to bring)

sections.purpose: Where the venue is, with directions.
alternatives: pin-map: when several places matter (venue, hotels, shuttle stops)

sections.purpose: How to get there (airport, transfer, shuttle) and hotels with room-block codes.
fields: Nearest airport or station and travel time
Hotels: name, distance, price per night, room-block code, booking deadline

sections.purpose: The dress code with do's and don'ts (ground, weather, colours to avoid).

fields: Registry link, fund description or 'no gifts'
How to ask for transfer details

sections.purpose: Children, plus-ones, accessibility, weather plan, photography, deadlines.

pages.purpose: Reply per guest: find the invitation by name, accept or decline for each person, add a plus-one when allowed, choose meals and note dietary needs, then extras.

sections.purpose: Reply-by date and what the form will ask.
A stepped reply: find invitation → who is coming → dinner → extras and a note, with a reply card filling in beside it.
fields: Guest list grouped by invitation, with plus-one allowance and children
Dietary options (vegetarian, vegan, allergies) and a free-text field
Extras to ask about (shuttle, welcome evening, brunch, song request)
sections.notes: Group each guest's fields in a fieldset with the guest's name as legend. Skip the dinner step when nobody is coming. Gentle hints when a meal clashes with a dietary choice. The live reply card is a role="status" region. On submit, confirm in a status region and offer 'Add to calendar' (an .ics download) and 'change my reply'.

content: Names of the couple and hosts
Date, time and time zone of each event across the days
Venue name, address, map location, parking and access
Photos of the couple and the venue, with alt text
Travel: nearest airport / station, shuttle times and stops
Hotels with distance, price range, room-block codes and deadlines
Dress code and do's and don'ts
Guest list by invitation, with plus-one allowance and children
Meal choices and dietary options; RSVP deadline
A named contact for guest questions

styles.name: stationery serif
styles.why: Ivory page, a script-free serif, hairline small caps and one muted green; arched photo frames and pill buttons; the invitation is set line by line. Suits a garden or countryside wedding.

styles.name: modern minimal
styles.why: Clean grotesk, lots of white and black-and-white photos; for a city ceremony or a small celebration.

pitfalls: Guest names and dietary or health details are personal data: keep the RSVP behind the invitation lookup, collect only what is needed and say how long it is kept.
Letting anyone browse the guest list: the lookup should match one invitation, never list names.
Dates and times without the day of the week or time zone for travelling guests; the date shown only inside a countdown.
Plus-ones offered to everyone because the form does not know each invitation's allowance.
RSVP fields not grouped per guest, so screen-reader users cannot tell whose meal they are choosing.
Hotel room-block codes and deadlines missing or out of date.
Heavy animations with no reduced-motion fallback on a site older relatives will open on old phones.
